title: Quick check: Coverage, CI, and Test Maintenance

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Coverage, CI, and Test Maintenance”?
options: The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Measuring coverage should verify what the learner can observe with repeatable tests, including a failure case.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
questions.answer_key: Measuring coverage should verify what the learner can observe with repeatable tests, including a failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Coverage, CI, and Test Maintenance: Measuring coverage should verify what the learner can observe with repeatable tests, including a failure case.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Measuring coverage?
options: Assert through roles, labels, and visible results rather than component internals.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
questions.answer_key: Assert through roles, labels, and visible results rather than component internals.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Coverage, CI, and Test Maintenance: Assert through roles, labels, and visible results rather than component internals.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Coverage, CI, and Test Maintenance” complete?
options: Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Coverage, CI, and Test Maintenance: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
